data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Vitamins & trace elements_

**Class:** Mineral supplement (ferrous sulfate, fumarate, gluconate; IV iron sucrose, ferric carboxymaltose)

## Mechanism of action
- Restores haemoglobin and tissue iron; iron is a cofactor for ribonucleotide reductase in rapidly dividing hair matrix cells

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Iron deficiency in telogen effluvium and female pattern hair loss (many experts aim for ferritin >40–70 ng/mL)
- Koilonychia, angular cheilitis, glossitis, pruritus of iron deficiency, Plummer–Vinson syndrome
- Iron deficiency from chronic blood loss (e.g. dermatitis herpetiformis/coeliac, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia)

## Dose & formulations
- Oral elemental iron 60–120 mg once daily or on alternate days (better absorption), with vitamin C, away from tea/calcium; continue 3 months after Hb normalises
- IV iron for intolerance or malabsorption

## Adverse effects
- GI upset, constipation, black stools; IV — hypersensitivity, skin staining at infusion site (brown pigmentation from extravasation)

## Contraindications
- Haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, haemolytic anaemia without iron deficiency

## Drug interactions
- Reduces absorption of tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, levothyroxine, dolutegravir, mycophenolate; PPIs/antacids reduce iron absorption

## Monitoring
- Hb, ferritin, transferrin saturation

## Pregnancy & lactation
Recommended in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Check ferritin in diffuse hair loss
- Separate iron from tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones

_Sources: Khopkar (Trace elements — iron); Wolverton 4e ch.40. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
